intro: On a Friday evening in Chicago, candles are lit in apartments in West Rogers Park and in houses in Highland Park. On Saturday morning a Torah scroll is carried through a synagogue in Skokie, and on a weeknight two students argue over a page of Talmud. Each of these scenes draws on texts and practices that are many centuries old. This unit studies Judaism, the religion of the Jewish people, through its own texts, its practices and its long history.

Chapter 7 looks at Jewish belief and practice: the covenant, the Shema, the Sabbath, the yearly cycle of holidays, the laws of kosher food and the ceremonies that mark birth, coming of age, marriage and death. Chapter 8 follows Jewish life through history: the fall of the Second Temple, the rabbis who rebuilt Judaism around study and prayer, the Mishnah and the Talmud, life under Islam and in Christian Europe, the modern movements, the Holocaust, the State of Israel and the diaspora, and Jewish Chicago.

Throughout, you will see that Jews disagree with one another, and that their tradition records those disagreements rather than hiding them. By the end you will be able to explain key Jewish terms, read a short passage from the Torah or the Talmud and say how different Jewish communities interpret it, and describe how one people kept its identity across two thousand years and many lands.
bigQuestion: How have Jews kept a covenant, a body of texts and a way of life alive through centuries of change, exile and argument?

timeline.t: Babylonians destroy the First Temple; many Judeans are exiled to Babylon
The Second Temple is completed in Jerusalem

Roman armies destroy the Second Temple
Rabbi Judah the Prince completes the Mishnah
The Babylonian Talmud reaches its final form

words.d: a binding agreement; in Jewish tradition, the bond between God and Israel with duties on both sides
the declaration from Deuteronomy 6:4 that God is one, recited morning and evening
a commandment; tradition counts 613 in the Torah; in everyday speech also a good deed
Jewish law, the path for how to keep the commandments, drawn from Torah, Talmud and later rulings
the Sabbath, from Friday sunset to Saturday nightfall, a day of rest, prayer and family
fit or proper; food prepared according to the Jewish dietary laws, called kashrut
repentance; literally return, the focus of the Days of Awe before Yom Kippur
son of the commandment; a Jewish boy at thirteen, responsible for the commandments (for girls, bat mitzvah)
a Jewish teacher and scholar of Torah and Jewish law; the word means my teacher

test.q: Which line is the Shema, the central Jewish declaration about God?
choices: Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one
Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy
For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice
How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people
test.why: The Shema comes from Deuteronomy 6:4 and declares that God is one. The others come from Exodus, Hosea and Lamentations.

test.q: In Jewish tradition, what is a covenant?
choices: A binding agreement between God and Israel with obligations on both sides
A law code written by Maimonides
test.why: At Sinai, Israel promises to keep the commandments and God promises to be Israel's God; that two-sided bond is the covenant.

test.q: Which holiday is a twenty-five-hour fast devoted to atonement?
test.why: Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, ends the Days of Awe with a full fast and a day of prayer.

test.q: Why will a Sabbath-observant Jew walk two miles to synagogue but not drive two blocks?
choices: Driving is forbidden only in Israel
The rabbis' categories of forbidden work measure creative change, not effort, and driving falls under them
test.why: The Mishnah's thirty-nine categories of labor define Sabbath work by creative change, such as kindling, not by how tiring a task is.

choices: The ordered Passover meal that retells the exodus using the Haggadah
The Saturday night ceremony that ends the Sabbath
The canopy at a Jewish wedding
The daily page of Talmud study
test.why: Seder means order; the Passover seder follows the Haggadah to tell the story of the exodus from Egypt.

test.q: Which pair of foods could NOT be served together at a kosher meal?
test.why: Kashrut forbids mixing meat and dairy, based on the verse about a kid in its mother's milk.

test.q: At what age does a Jewish boy become a bar mitzvah under Jewish law?
test.why: At thirteen a boy becomes responsible for the commandments; eight days is the age for brit milah.

test.q: After the Temple fell in 70 CE, which town became a center for rebuilding Jewish life?
test.why: According to rabbinic tradition, Yohanan ben Zakkai asked for Yavneh and its sages, and the rabbis gathered there.

test.q: The Talmud is made up of:
test.why: The Talmud joins the Mishnah, edited around 200 CE, to the Gemara, the later rabbinic discussion of it.

test.q: Why does the Talmud record the views of the House of Shammai even though the law follows Hillel?
choices: Shammai's views became law in Babylonia
The printers could not remove them
It treats both as words of the living God and honors argument for the sake of heaven
test.why: The Talmud's heavenly voice says these and these are the words of the living God, and Pirkei Avot praises argument for the sake of heaven.

test.q: Which statement about Orthodox, Conservative and Reform Judaism is accurate?
choices: Only Orthodox Jews keep the Sabbath in any form
Reform Judaism began in the United States in 1950
They differ on how binding Jewish law is and whether it can change
test.why: Orthodox Jews see halakhah as unchanging, Conservative Jews as binding but developing, and Reform Jews as guidance for informed choice.

test.q: What happened to the Jews of Spain in 1492?
choices: Those who would not convert were ordered to leave
They were moved into the first ghetto
test.why: Ferdinand and Isabella ordered all Jews who would not convert to leave Spain; many settled in the Ottoman Empire.

test.q: Holocaust Remembrance Day in Jewish communities is called:
test.why: Yom HaShoah, each spring, remembers the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust. Tisha B'Av mourns the Temples.

test.q: Ladino is to Sephardi Jews as Yiddish is to:
test.why: Yiddish, a German-based language, was the everyday language of Ashkenazi Jews in Central and Eastern Europe.

test.q: What does the word diaspora refer to?
choices: Jewish communities living outside the land of Israel
test.why: Diaspora, from a Greek word for scattering, names Jewish communities outside the land of Israel.

write.prompt: Is Judaism held together more by its texts or by its practices? Cite at least two texts from this unit, such as Deuteronomy 6:4, Exodus 20:8–10, Hosea 6:6 or Hillel's answer in Shabbat 31a, and explain how different Jewish communities would answer and why.
tips: Name each text you cite by book and verse, or by tractate and page.
Attribute every belief: write the Talmud teaches or Orthodox Jews hold, not it is true that.
Show diversity within Judaism: Orthodox, Conservative, Reform and Reconstructionist answers may differ.
Use the unit's terms, such as covenant, halakhah, mitzvah and Talmud, and define each briefly.
Compare and explain; do not judge which answer is better.
